questions.question_text:
A colony of bacteria begins with $600$ organisms and increases by $20\%$ each hour.
How many bacteria are present after $3$ hours, to the nearest whole number?

options.why: Added simple percentage growth $600 + 3(0.20 \times 600) = 960$ instead of compounding.
Evaluated $600(1.20)^4$, calculating for $4$ hours instead of $3$.
Calculated the population after only $1$ hour: $600 \times 1.20 = 720$.

questions.question_text:
A machine purchased for $\$18\,000$ depreciates at a reducing-balance rate of $15\%$ per annum.
What is its salvage value after $2$ years?

options.why: Subtracted flat linear depreciation of $30\%$ ($2 \times 15\%$) of $\$18\,000$.
Calculated the value after only $1$ year: $\$18\,000 \times 0.85$.
Calculated the value after $3$ years instead of $2$: $18000(0.85)^3=11054.25$, giving $\$11\,054.25$.

questions.question_text:
A medical isotope has an initial radioactivity of $640\text{ MBq}$.
If its activity decays by $50\%$ every $4$ hours, what is its radioactivity after $12$ hours?

options.why: Calculated activity after $2$ half-life periods ($8$ hours) instead of $3$.
Calculated activity after $4$ half-life periods ($16$ hours).
Applied the decay factor only once: $640(0.5)=320$, instead of applying it for all $3$ periods.

questions.question_text:
An initial investment of $\$4000$ grows at $7\%$ per annum compounded annually.
After how many complete years will its year-end value first exceed $\$10\,000$?

options.why: Truncated the threshold $\ln(2.5)/\ln(1.07)\approx13.54$ instead of choosing the first complete year exceeding it.
Used flat growth of $\$280$ each year: $(10000-4000)/280\approx21.43$, then chose $22$ years.
Added an unnecessary extra year after correctly finding that $14$ complete years already exceeds the target.

questions.question_text:
A radioactive sample has an initial mass of $10\text{ g}$.
Its mass decreases by $20\%$ each day.
What mass remains after $3$ days?

options.why: Calculated the mass after $2$ days: $10(0.8)^2=6.4\text{ g}$.
Calculated the mass after $4$ days: $10(0.8)^4=4.096\text{ g}$.
Subtracted $20\%$ of the initial mass each day: $10-3(0.20\times10)=4\text{ g}$, using a linear model.

questions.question_text:
A vehicle bought for $\$25\,000$ depreciates to $\$16\,000$ after $2$ years under the reducing balance method.
What is the annual depreciation rate $d$?

options.why: Calculated total $2$-year loss $36\%$ instead of the annual rate $d$.
Divided the total $36\%$ depreciation by $2$ linearly instead of taking the geometric root.
Found the first-year value as $\$20\,000$ but divided the first-year loss by that remaining value instead of the initial value: $(25000-20000)/20000\times100=25\%$.

questions.question_text:
A population of fish in a lake decreases by $10\%$ each year.
After how many full years will the population first fall below half of its initial size?

options.why: Calculated $50\% / 10\% = 5$ years using a linear reduction model.
Truncated $6.58$ instead of rounding up to the next full year where it first falls below half.
Calculated the doubling time of a growing population instead of decay.

questions.question_text:
An invasive weed covers an area of $50\text{ m}^{2}$ and expands by $25\%$ every $2$ weeks.
What area will the weed cover after $10$ weeks (to the nearest $\text{m}^{2}$)?

options.why: Used $n = 10$ periods instead of $n = 5$ two-week periods.
Used linear growth: $50+5(0.25\times50)=112.5$, which rounds to $113\text{ m}^{2}$.
Used only $4$ growth periods: $50(1.25)^4=122.0703125$, which rounds to $122\text{ m}^{2}$.
